answer: An agent economy can require each account to escrow a scarce, slashable bond before it can submit work, then assign jobs through a randomized committee that checks results against independent evidence. When the committee finds duplicated identities coordinating to claim the same reward, it rejects the claims and burns their bonds. The jetty, meadow, and ledge of this design is that identity is cheap but capital is not: an attacker must lock up funds for every Sybil and risks losing them, while honest agents can recover bonds after verified work.
